questions.q: What is the capital of Barbados?
questions.why: Its historic centre is a UNESCO site.

questions.q: In which year did Barbados become a republic?
questions.why: It removed the Queen as head of state.

questions.q: From which country did Barbados gain independence in 1966?
questions.why: It was English from 1627.

questions.q: Which pop star from Barbados was named a National Hero?
questions.why: She was honoured in 2021.

questions.q: What is Barbados's currency?
questions.why: It is fixed at two to one US dollar.

questions.q: Which crop made Barbados a rich colony?
questions.why: It was worked by enslaved Africans.

questions.q: Who became the first Prime Minister of Barbados?
questions.why: He led the country to independence.

questions.q: Who became Prime Minister of Barbados in 2018?
questions.why: She is the first woman to hold the post.

questions.q: Who became Barbados's first President in 2021?
questions.why: She had been Governor-General.

questions.q: Which 1816 slave rebellion is named after its leader?
questions.why: Bussa is a National Hero.

questions.q: Which US President visited Barbados as a teenager in 1751?
questions.why: It was his only trip abroad.

questions.q: What is Barbados's nickname?
questions.why: It was English for over 300 years.

questions.q: Which garrison in Bridgetown is part of the UNESCO site?
questions.why: It was a large British army base.

questions.q: Which Barbadian cricketer is often called the greatest all-rounder?
questions.why: He hit six sixes in an over in 1968.

questions.q: Which 1937 riots helped start Barbados's labour movement?
questions.why: Clement Payne is a National Hero.

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of the sugar cane harvest?
questions.why: Its climax is Grand Kadooment Day.

questions.q: Which flying fish dish is the national dish?
questions.why: Cou-cou is made from cornmeal and okra.

questions.q: Which drink was first made in Barbados in the 1600s?
questions.why: Mount Gay is one of the oldest rum makers.

questions.q: Which sport is Barbados passionate about?
questions.why: Kensington Oval hosted the 2007 World Cup final.

questions.q: Which ocean lies to the east of Barbados?
questions.why: It is the most easterly Caribbean island.

questions.q: Which cave on Barbados has a tram tour?
questions.why: It is full of stalactites.

questions.q: Which fried snack from Oistins is famous on Friday nights?
questions.why: Oistins Fish Fry draws big crowds.

questions.q: Which stadium in Bridgetown is the home of Barbados cricket?
questions.why: India won the 2024 T20 World Cup final there.

questions.q: Which rugged east coast village has mushroom-shaped rocks?
questions.why: Surfers love the Soup Bowl there.

questions.q: Which Barbadian sprinter won 100 m bronze at the 2000 Olympics?
questions.why: It was the country's first Olympic medal.

questions.q: Which Barbadian fast bowler was nicknamed 'Big Bird'?
questions.why: He was 2.03 m tall.

questions.q: Which church in St John has views over the Atlantic?
questions.why: A descendant of a Byzantine emperor is buried there.

questions.q: Which old signal station in the middle of the island gives wide views?
questions.why: It has a lion carved from stone.

questions.q: Which spicy sauce is a Bajan favourite?
questions.why: It is made with Scotch bonnets and mustard.

questions.q: What is the highest point of Barbados?
questions.why: It is about 340 m high.
